subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should shared-workspace dreaming be fixed as default per-agent isolation, or should maintainers accept the open allowlist/config approach as the first supported boundary?
rationale: The bug has a clear source-level isolation failure, but the active implementation path adds public config/API surface and may not fully cover default shared-workspace isolation; that security boundary needs maintainer intent before a repair lane duplicates or redirects the work.

options.title: Default Agent Isolation
options.body: Treat cross-agent dreaming as a bug and require the fix to isolate by current agent by default, with any opt-in pooling/config handled separately.

options.title: Accept Allowlist First
options.body: Accept the open PR’s allowlist as the first durable control, while keeping this issue or a follow-up open for true shared-workspace default isolation.

options.title: Pause For Broader Memory Isolation
options.body: Defer this issue behind the broader multi-agent memory isolation/security track if maintainers want one unified storage and tool boundary design.

recommendation.title: Default Agent Isolation
recommendation.body: Treat cross-agent dreaming as a bug and require the fix to isolate by current agent by default, with any opt-in pooling/config handled separately.

likelyOwner.reason: This user is assigned, has already narrowed the issue in comments, and has recent adjacent memory-core history.
